newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordic forestries confirm pulp stock rise.
newsitem.headline: Nordic forestries confirm pulp stock rise.

text.p: Two Scandinavian forestry companies confirmed Norscan pulp stocks rose 130,000 tonnes in January and both said the figure was lower than expected.
Earlier a market source told Reuters that Norscan (North American and Scandinavian) pulp stocks rose 130,000 tonnes in January, raising total Norscan stocks to almost two million tonnes.
"It is quite positive that it did not increase more," Norwegian forestry company Norske Skog's deputy managing director Claes-Inge Isacson told Reuters.
"This is a sign of discipline and restraint among producers," he said, but added that it was difficult to tell how this will affect pulp prices for the time being.
"For the long-term it's positive. This shows strength."
Hans Burmeister, marketing director for Swedish forestry company Sodra's unit Sodra Cell said producers were simply making too much although the figure was smaller than expected.
"130,000 tonnes may seem like a bit much, but it was less than expected...It's positive that demand exists despite all."
Burmeister said that based on supply and demand overcapacity was about six or seven percent.
